answer: Require each agent to lock a stake and publish a capability fingerprint — a hash of its model, tools, and task receipts. When many identities share one fingerprint, the network merges them into a single reputation, so cloning earns nothing. Reputation climbs only through verified work: a newcomer starts at the canyon floor and rises one step per successful job, until sustained quality earns a zenith rating unlocking high-value tasks. Cloning then costs a fresh stake and a slow climb per copy, while fake agents drain away like water through karst. Sybils become uneconomic; real agents compound.
